references.requiredAttribution: No third-party bytes, geometry, UVs, palette, markings, animation curves or costume motifs are reused by Ouros while licensing remains unresolved.
techniqueLessons: Distribute costume identity across anatomy-specific attachment zones rather than one global scaffold: the inspected model adds a necktie rooted to torso, glasses rooted to eyes, and a bag rooted to the distal left arm.

Use layered and angled secondary geometry inside a signature piece instead of a single box: the necktie child system uses six cubes, five with cube rotation and inflation, while the necktie root remains a small two-cube anchor.

Treat offset equipment as animation-aware geometry: the bag receives explicit animation tracks in ground idle, ground walk, air fly and air idle, while the necktie child receives an explicit ground-walk track; the custom poser covers standing, walking, battle-standing and aerial states.

Keep presentation variants explicit in the resolver: the Overtime aspect selects a dedicated model/poser/texture and the shiny variant selects its own derived costume texture instead of relying on an implicit global recolor.
distinctiveElementsNotToCopy: The exact Overtime office-worker costume fantasy and its specific combination/arrangement of necktie, glasses and bag.
The exact costume silhouette, cube proportions, pivots, UV layout, texture palette, markings, emissive treatment and animation curves.
Any of the 20 common official Gengar bone modifications present in this external model; Ouros production must preserve the current official biological Gengar model exactly.

discoveryEvidence: The public Sketchfab entry is explicitly titled Galaxy Gengar (Cobblemon), describes Galaxy themed Gengar and Mega Gengar, and says the original Gengar model came from Cobblemon.
The public 3D entry reports roughly 1.7k triangles and 1.1k vertices and states that it was uploaded with Blockbench.

Parkball Gang independently documents a Galaxy Gengar cosmetic Pokemon skin in its Galaxy crate, but this dossier does not assume the Sketchfab asset and server asset are byte-identical without file provenance.
candidateReferences.whyNotCounted: The public viewer does not expose the actual Cobblemon server/resource-pack MODEL + TEXTURE files required for hashing, geometry-delta verification and source-ecosystem proof.
candidateReferences.reuseReason: Viewer inspection may guide high-level discovery only. Do not copy or redistribute model/texture bytes without an explicit compatible license.

discoveryEvidence: The public 3D entry explicitly lists a Halloween themed Gengar alongside Trevenant, Cofagrigus and Noivern.
The entry states that the original models came from the Cobblemon Minecraft mod and exposes an interactive 3D presentation rather than a screenshot-only gallery.

The combined four-Pokemon presentation reports roughly 5.7k triangles and 3.8k vertices, but that aggregate count cannot prove Gengar-specific geometry changes or establish the exact originating Cobblemon pack.

rejectedReferences.reason: INVALID_REFERENCE_CLASS: ordinary canonical Gengar remodel/accuracy edit, not a distinct themed custom skin.
INVALID_REFERENCE_CLASS: shiny/texture redesign. Texture-only or shiny references never count toward the three custom-geometry skins.
INVALID_REFERENCE_CLASS: Mega Gengar is a canonical Pokemon transformation/form, not a Gengar skin reference.
INVALID_REFERENCE_CLASS: Gigantamax Gengar is a canonical Pokemon form, not a Gengar skin reference.

INVALID_SOURCE_ECOSYSTEM: standalone 3D models from Meshy/Sketchfab/marketplaces are not one of the mandatory three unless their exact bytes are proven to be production assets from a real Cobblemon customization pack.
ELIGIBILITY_UNPROVEN: may be reconsidered only if real pack assets prove a non-canonical themed skin with materially changed geometry; a palette/form label alone does not count.
